audit.whatIsWrong: Not one K'Sante ability is named on the page (flagged in the packet defects), and the two mechanics it does describe are both wrong: it calls his Q a 'knockup' you should bait, and it says an All-Out K'Sante chases you 'through his W block'.
audit.why: Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5-second flat cooldown that damages and slows in a line and grants a stack — 'At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that PULLS enemies in.' It is a pull, not a knockup, and at 3.5s there is no cooldown to bait: what you read is his stack count, because only the second one displaces. And Path Maker's own text says 'When All Out, deals increased damage and NO LONGER knocks back or stuns' — so the moment he ults, the ability the page tells you to fear stops being able to move you at all.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named. Ntofo Strikes re-described as a 3.5s stack builder whose second cast pulls; Path Maker's All-Out CC loss written into the late text, whys[5], the don'ts and Key Ability Interactions.

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out is described only as 'strips his own resists for raw AD'. The wall interaction and the healing are missing.
audit.why: Riot: 'K'Sante knocks an enemy back, LAUNCHING THEM THROUGH ANY WALL in their path. Then, K'Sante goes All Out and dashes after them, gaining increased damage, HEALING, and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defenses.' 120/100/80 at 250 range. Standing next to terrain is how you get thrown into his jungle, and the healing is the anti-heal trigger _missing-interactions.json flags for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Wall launch written into the first-item spike and the late text as a positioning rule; the healing tied to Oblivion Orb timing in itemization and the late block; 120s cooldown carried through.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer keys the entire lane off 'the All Out cooldown', which is a level-6 ultimate, and gives no number for anything.
audit.why: Through levels 1-5 the ability that decides trades is Path Maker at 14/13/12/11/10 — the charge takes reduced damage and the dash knocks back and stuns. All Out is 120s and does not exist until 6. Footwork is 10s and only gets its longer range when he targets an ALLY, so in a solo lane it is the short version.
audit.corrected: 14s Path Maker, 10s Footwork, 3.5s Ntofo Strikes and 120s All Out written into the cooldown block, the do's, the trading rules and the loading tip so the lane-phase advice keys off the right ability.

audit.why: The content layer's stage read is honest and matches the on-disk 47.55% over 1365 games: he owns 1-2 and both item stages, Galio gets a narrow level-3 window and a level-6 map spike rather than a kill spike. I only made the mechanics behind those judgements specific.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Oblivion Orb early — his healing fights your trade math' names no source or timing.
audit.why: His only heal is All Out itself, so the Orb does nothing before level 6 and everything after — and because All Out also reduces his own defences, the ult window is simultaneously when he heals most and when your damage lands hardest.
audit.corrected: Itemization now names All Out as the heal and marks the ult window as the moment your damage and his healing both spike.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 swing back to him — his W blocks your key cast and his percent-HP ability damage plus stat lead win any extended trade you start, so don't channel a slow Shield of Durand into a healthy K'Sante who can just block the release. Level 6 is your one spike and it's a map spike, not a lane spike: Hero's Entrance won't reliably solo-kill him, but it lets you flag onto a sidelane or a fight and win the game off pressure you generate elsewhere. Treat lane as a holding action and cash 6 in on the rest of the map.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 swing back to him — Path Maker stuns you out of the Shield of Durand release and Dauntless Instinct marks you for bonus damage on his next attack, so never start a slow channel into a K'Sante still holding his W. Footwork is his other out, 10s, and it only gets long range when he dashes to an ally, so in lane it is the short version. Level 6 is your spike and it is a map spike: Hero's Entrance won't solo him, but it wins the game elsewhere. Treat lane as a holding action.

Stop duelling — group, flag onto fights, and let the taunt-knockup decide 5v5s.

notes: The packet flagged this page for never naming a single K'Sante ability, and the two mechanics it did describe were both wrong. (1) It called his Q a 'knockup' to bait. Ntofo Strikes is a 3.5-second flat cooldown — nothing to bait — and its crowd control is a PULL that only fires on the second stack, so the reader should be counting stacks. (2) It said an All-Out K'Sante 'chases you through his W block'. Riot's Path Maker text says the opposite: 'When All Out, deals increased damage and NO LONGER knocks back or stuns.' His displacement disappears the instant he ults, which is genuinely useful and the page had it inverted. Also added: All Out 'launch[es] them through any wall in their path', so where you stand relative to terrain decides whether his ult is a knockback or a relocation into his jungle; and All Out is his only heal, which fixes the vague Oblivion Orb line. NOT WRITTEN: _missing-interactions.json claims 'K'Sante bypasses stacking resistances (Path Maker (W)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here', derived from a trueDamage flag on Path Maker. Riot's Path Maker description contains no true-damage clause, so per the kit-file rule I trusted the description and left the resistance-bypass claim off the page; the armour build direction is unchanged.
